result:
The proposed answer of 185 is almost certainly wrong. Its claim that connectivity is needed for every pair, including (89, 97), is too strong, so the lower bound is not valid.

**Pairs involving an uncovered prime.** Suppose S misses some residue class mod a prime q. Then Banana can pick f with period q that is constant on S but nonconstant overall. That constant data is also consistent with any other prime p for which S does not cover all residues. So for every pair of primes, at least one must have S covering all of its residues. Hence at most one prime can be left uncovered, and the natural choice is 97.

**Connectivity for covered pairs.** For two covered primes p and q, the bipartite graph on residues mod p and mod q, with an edge for each element of S, must be connected. If it is disconnected, Banana can assign different values to different components. That gives data consistent with both periods and nonconstant. Connectivity requires at least p + q − 1 edges. The worst case among primes up to 89 is (83, 89), which gives n ≥ 171.

**The uncovered prime 97.** Take all elements of S congruent to 0 mod 97. Then any data from period 97 is constant. Any data consistent with a covered prime p is nonconstant, since S covers every residue mod p and f is nonconstant. So 97 is distinguished from every other prime automatically. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, the remaining conditions reduce to the primes up to 89, so the bound 171 appears to be achievable. I did not construct such a set explicitly. This matches my recollection that the known answer is 171.

The proposed 185 arises from requiring the full pair (89, 97) to be covered and connected, which is unnecessary. The correct answer is 171, not 185.

VERDICT: REJECT
